text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves nothing. All-female panels occur routinely, often because HR and senior functions are staffed that way, and the makeup of a panel says nothing about how it weighed candidates. Leading with it signals grievance rather than substance and will harden attitudes against you.

Your stronger ground is concrete: paper credentials that look, on their face, more specialised than the successful candidate's, plus an unanswered request for written reasons. Chase that in writing, cite any internal policy or statutory deadline, and ask specifically how the criteria were scored.

If the scoring reveals criteria invented after the fact or applied inconsistently, you then have something real. Note also that "regulatory affairs" experience may genuinely have been the priority.
